THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER 1.

Accused nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.40/2024 registered by Nagara Police Station, Shivamogga, for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498A, 149 IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, are before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.PC seeking anticipatory bail.

2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.40/2024 was registered by Nagara Police Station, Shivamogga, against the petitioners herein and another for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 26.07.2024 received from Akshata Kalahal who is the wife of accused no.1.
Apprehending arrest in the NC: 2024:KHC:37494 C/W CRL.P.Nos.9225/2024, said case, petitioners had filed applications before the jurisdictional Sessions Court seeking anticipatory bail.
The said applications were rejected by the Sessions Court, and therefore, the petitioners are before this Court.
4. Learned Counsel for the petitioners having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, submits that the relationship between accused no.1 and his wife is strained.
The alleged offences are triable by the Court of Magistrate and the maximum punishment for the same is imprisonment for a period of three years.
Petitioner are ready and willing to cooperate with the police for the purpose of investigation.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petitions.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petitions.
6. Perusal of the material available on record would go to show that the marriage of accused no.1 and the first informant was solemnized on 27.01.2022.
It is appears that subsequently their relationship got strained and the first informant was suspecting that accused no.1 had illicit relationship with accused no.4.

The first information is now filed alleging that NC: 2024:KHC:37494 C/W CRL.P.Nos.9225/2024, accused persons were ill-treating and torturing the first informant in her matrimonial house and were also demanding additional dowry from her.
It is also alleged that accused no.1 has illicit relationship with accused no.4.
Petitioners do not have criminal antecedents.
The alleged offences are triable by the Court of Magistrate and the maximum punishment for the said offences is imprisonment for a period of three years.
Petitioners have undertaken to cooperate with the police for the purpose of investigation.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioners prayer for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:
7.
The petitions are allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioners in the event of their arrest in Crime No.40/2024 registered by Nagara Police Station, Shivamogga, for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498A, 149 IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, subject to the following conditions:
NC: 2024:KHC:37494 C/W CRL.P.Nos.9225/2024,
1.

The Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
each with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioners shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioners shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and they shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
4. The petitioners shall not involve in similar offences in future.

SD/- 
(S VISHWAJITH SHETTY) JUDGE KK Shri. Narendra Kalahal vs State Of Karnataka on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29779380/
